title: Fox at the Gate — variant 1 (requested 108 BPM) score

ground_truth.key_intro: D major (dominant vamp, same as the master)

unintended_differences: Suno did not change the tempo: measured 96.564 BPM, not 108. Autocorrelation is +0.41 at 96 BPM and -0.13 at 108 BPM. 39 of 40 local 8-beat windows sit near 96; none sit near 108. Even a 108 BPM beat-tracker prior still returns 95.703.
Duration stayed 108.680 s (master 108.400 s, +0.280 s) instead of shrinking to about 96.4 s.
Lyric and section times are essentially the same as the master (start deltas under 0.11 s), not scaled by 96/108.
Beat grid is less stable: IBI CV 4.72% (medium) vs 1.54% (high) on the master. First tracked beat is at 0.116 s vs 1.045 s.
Loudness: integrated -15.8 vs -15.3 LUFS; LRA 3.2 vs 4.8 LU; true peak -2.0 vs -3.1 dBFS; side/mid energy 0.028 vs 0.087 (narrower stereo).
Structural novelty is busier and does not land cleanly on the lyric boundaries, unlike the master's peaks at 9.752 s and 30.070 s.

fox_ears.scoring_rule: Tempo is a hit within ±4% (octave and 3:2 forgiven); key must match exactly. Score against the measured 96.564 BPM / G major truth, not the 108 BPM prompt.

before_default.tempo_note: unresolved metrical level — pulse candidates 180/90 BPM; autocorrelation suggests 120 BPM
before_default.tempo_verdict: miss vs 96.564 (6.80% low). Same miss, and almost the same number, as on the master (90 BPM).
before_default.subgrid_proposal_verdict: hit under ±4% (1.49% high vs 96.564). Master proposal was 94 BPM.
before_default.key_verdict: miss (same intro-dominant trap as the master, which was D major 0.88)
before_default.vocal_verdict: miss (same as the master: 4.1% gate, 0 vocal notes)

after_pass1.tempo_note: sub-grid onsets (345); comb x prior picked 96 BPM; nearest rival level 192 BPM at 42%
after_pass1.tempo_verdict: hit. Reports 96, not 108. Ratio to its own master reading (96/96) is 1.00, not 1.125. That is the correct answer, because the audio did not change tempo.
after_pass1.key_note: tonic-vs-dominant: D vs G unresolved; kept the profile winner
after_pass1.key_verdict: miss. On the master, pass 1 correctly said G major (0.86) with 'G over D confirmed'. This is a false difference: both renders are G major.
after_pass1.sections_verdict: partial. The five true boundaries are found (errors under 0.8 s), but three extra mid-section cuts appear (19.7 mid verse 1, 43.5 mid chorus 1, 88.5 mid chorus 2) on top of the mid-verse-2 cut already seen on the master (64.8). Count is 10 vs 7 on the master vs 6 in the truth. Role labels also start at 'verse' instead of 'intro'.
after_pass1.vocal_verdict: hit, close to the master (P 0.92 / R 0.72). The vocal is still heard; no false 'vocals vanished' report.

fox_ears.reason: There was no tempo change in the audio to catch. Pass 1 correctly kept tempo at 96 BPM and did not invent a 108 BPM reading. It did report two false differences vs its own master reading: key flipped from G major to D major, and the form split from 7 sections to 10.
false_differences_vs_its_master_reading: Key: G major (0.86) on the master → D major (0.84) on this variant. Truth is G major both times. The tonic-vs-dominant check went from 'G over D confirmed' to 'D vs G unresolved; kept the profile winner'.
Sections: 7 → 10, with new mid-verse-1, mid-chorus-1 and mid-chorus-2 cuts. Wall-clock form is the same as the master.
new_tuning_issues: Tonic-vs-dominant key check is unstable across two same-key, same-form Suno renders. A new take of the same G-major song with the same D-major intro vamp can flip the winner back to the dominant.
Section splitter over-segments more on this take (10 vs 7 vs 6 truth), inventing mid-phrase cuts in both verses and both choruses. Role labels are also wrong.

This file is not a valid 108 BPM test. A later render, or a controlled time-stretch of the master to 108 BPM, is needed before we can say whether Fox Ears tracks a real tempo change and only that change.
